### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. COG6-congenital disorder of glycosylation  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.485)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6811440, Reactome:R-HSA-6807878, Reactome:R-HSA-6811438)

**Proposed mechanism:** COG8 (HGNC:2176) —DISRUPTS→ COG complex function (GO:0035570); COG6 (HGNC:2173) —DISRUPTS→ COG complex function (GO:0035570); COG complex function (GO:0035570) —LEADS_TO→ N-linked glycosylation (GO:0046787); N-linked glycosylation (GO:0046787) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital disorder of glycosylation (HP:0031729); N-linked glycosylation (GO:0046787) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal N-linked glycosylation (HP:0011337). Loss-of-function mutations in COG8 (MONDO:0012635) and COG6 (MONDO:0013810) both disrupt the function of the COG complex, a key regulator of N-linked glycosylation. This disruption leads to a generalized defect in N-linked glycosylation, manifesting as congenital disorder of glycosylation phenotypes in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in COG8 or COG6 with a frequency greater than 1% in gnomAD would falsify the hypothesis that these genes are the primary causal agents for these specific rare diseases. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of disrupted N-linked glycosylation due to COG complex dysfunction could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting the glycosylation pathway or protein folding chaperones, potentially benefiting patients with either disease.

#### 2. COG5-congenital disorder of glycosylation  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.477)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6811440, Reactome:R-HSA-6807878, Reactome:R-HSA-6811438)

**Proposed mechanism:** COG8 (HGNC:2676) —DISRUPTS→ Vesicular transport to Golgi (GO:0006899); COG5 (HGNC:2673) —DISRUPTS→ Vesicular transport to Golgi (GO:0006899); Vesicular transport to Golgi (GO:0006899) —LEADS_TO→ Protein O-mannosylation (GO:0031400); Protein O-mannosylation (GO:0031400) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Protein O-mannosylation (GO:0031400) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal facial shape (HP:0001999); Protein O-mannosylation (GO:0031400) —LEADS_TO→ Global developmental delay (HP:0001263); Protein O-mannosylation (GO:0031400) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250). Loss-of-function mutations in either COG8 or COG5 disrupt the function of the COG complex, impairing vesicular transport to and within the Golgi apparatus. This leads to defects in protein O-mannosylation, a critical post-translational modification, which in turn results in a spectrum of neurodevelopmental and dysmorphic phenotypes common to both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in COG8 or COG5 with a minor allele frequency >0.1% in gnomAD for the respective disease population would cast doubt on their causal role. Alternatively, demonstrating distinct downstream molecular pathways for COG8 and COG5 defects, not converging on protein O-mannosylation, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: HG00731)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of impaired protein O-mannosylation in both diseases could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting glycosylation pathways or downstream consequences, potentially benefiting patients with either condition. Investigating the role of the COG complex in neurological development may reveal novel therapeutic targets.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of Golgi trafficking in these distinct neurodevelopmental disorders could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting common downstream pathways, such as enhancing protein folding or clearance, or improving vesicle transport, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
